capability_semantics: A non-zero vector dissolve requires cutly.transition-scope.vector-path-viewport-px.v1, cutly.vector.path-viewport-px.v2 and cutly.transition.dissolve.v1 in addition to every authored property/keyframe capability. The scoped token proves the backend implements their composition rather than merely supporting static vectors and video-only dissolves separately.
excluded_responsibilities: Text transitions, vector strokes or curves, SVG/CSS, motion interpolation inside the vector source, masks, non-dissolve transitions, provider/runtime attestation, encoding and publication remain outside this amendment.
failure_semantics: Unsupported vector profiles, cross-track or non-adjacent clips, disabled clips, mixed asset kinds, wrong transition role/scope/time, missing provider capability or any receipt mismatch fail closed. There is no edge-frame substitution or visible-time clamp.
handle_semantics: The active half-open dissolve window and complementary weights remain exactly cutly.evaluator.transition-dissolve.v1. Vector sources need no temporal media head or tail bytes, but a source provider must explicitly authorize the actual transition ID, role and out-of-visible handle time; clamping or substituting a visible clip time is forbidden.
provider_semantics: A transition-aware expression provider binds the complete document/timeline/track/transition/clip/asset scope, outgoing or incoming role, actual evaluator timeline/local/source time, intrinsic viewport, semantic source hash and full raster profile chain. The ordinary visible-clip provider contract remains unchanged.
scope_semantics: The existing dissolve profile may connect adjacent enabled clips on one TrackKindVector only when both clips reference AssetKindVector sources using cutly.vector.path-viewport-px.v2. Text tracks, legacy vector v1 and mixed track/source kinds remain invalid.
source_semantics: Both vector expressions are immutable intrinsic raster sources. At every active transition time the evaluator still computes each clip's exact timeline/local/source handle time and clip properties; only the source pixels are time-invariant.
